quests.title: Gig: Getting Warmer...
quests.synopsis: Wakako sends V to extract a trapped netrunner whose protective software makes forced disconnection dangerous.

stages.description: Wakako identifies the rescue target; this is a client report, not evidence that V has met her.
Reach the apartment and receive instructions through the runner’s screens.
Find coolant and apply it before detaching the neural link.
Detach the runner after the cooling step; outcome needs direct state confirmation.
Carry the unconscious runner to Wakako’s transport.

decisions.description: Whether the disconnection preserved 8ug8ear’s life.

outcomes.description: Coolant used before safe disconnection.
Unsafe disconnection killed the story runner.

runtime.notes: Require ordered cooling and disconnection branch evidence plus actor/outcome confirmation. A companion copy cannot prove story survival.

decisions.description: Whether a living rescue target reached transport.

outcomes.description: Living runner handed to the fixer’s driver.

runtime.notes: The patient was unconscious during physical evacuation; exact rescue actions are witnessed by V and learned by her through a credible later account, not automatically recalled as sights she saw.

uncertainties: The profile must not treat a screen exchange as a long face-to-face friendship.
No exact failure flag or time limit has been verified.

Speak after he recovers.

decisions.description: Whether Nam recovered and personally met V.

outcomes.description: Shard-assisted recovery followed by conversation.
Later availability as a quickhack vendor is observed.

runtime.notes: Recovery and vendor availability are distinct milestones; evaluate each explicitly rather than promoting a generic completed journal state.

uncertainties: Sources disagree on age (older gig briefing 65, later account 67); no age-dependent conclusions.
Uncompleted is not equivalent to dead or refused.

outcomes.description: V specifically recruited Nam for the intrusion.
Nam delivered the information and suffered aphasia after the hack.
V and Nam discussed leaving Night City after the injury.

runtime.notes: Only the selected runner knows this work firsthand. Discussion of departure is not verified arrival elsewhere, and aphasia is not an invitation to caricature speech.

uncertainties: Partial coverage: no convoy assault, Reed/Songbird outcome or other runner route is owned by this record.

outcomes.description: Iris’s vehicle was returned with her.
Iris was rescued but her vehicle/equipment was left behind.

uncertainties: Additional gratitude/reward does not establish romance, permanent employment or friendship.

quests.title: Every Breath You Take
quests.synopsis: Protect Blue Moon while identifying a stalker; mistaken success and later death must remain distinguishable.

stages.description: Blue Moon explains the harassment and protection plan.
Follow her around Kabuki without ruining the plan.
Investigate a suspicious fan and inspect evidence.
Prevent the attack and establish which person was stopped.
Check later messages, not just the immediate job label.

decisions.description: Whom V identified as the stalker.

outcomes.description: Evidence identifies Griselda Martinez, using the fan name Green Cloud.
V reported a different person as the culprit.

runtime.notes: Narrative meaning only. Exact native fact/journal paths, stage gates, version and branch evidence must be reviewed before runtime use. Missing facts and zero values establish no outcome.

decisions.description: Blue Moon’s verified safety during and after the operation.

outcomes.description: She survived the attack and debriefed after the correct intervention.
The stalker killed her during the operation.
A later report established her death after V misidentified the threat.
V left or compromised the operation; later survival still needs its own evidence.

runtime.notes: A completed journal entry does not guarantee survival; late messages and exact rescue branch are required. A summoned copy is never proof of resurrection.

decisions.description: How the confirmed attacker was stopped.

outcomes.description: The confirmed stalker was incapacitated and police handling discussed.
The confirmed stalker was killed.

runtime.notes: Differentiate intended arrest from confirmed police custody. Reward equality does not erase moral/emotional distinction.

decisions.description: The actual stalker was physically stopped; identity learned, lethal force and Blue Moon survival remain separate questions.

outcomes.description: The actual woman stalking Blue Moon was killed, defeated or rendered unconscious. This does not establish which of those occurred or whether her legal identity was learned.

runtime.notes: Narrative record. The reviewed native pack supplies a bounded positive predicate for actual neutralization, with V disclosure required; identity and lethal disposition are independent outcomes.

uncertainties: No canonical romance is established by gratitude or friendly messages.
Red Menace’s actions and survival need separate observations, not extrapolation from Blue Moon’s result.

quests.title: Violence

decisions.description: What V actually learned at Riot.

outcomes.description: V overheard the personality-copy proposal and obtained evidence.
Premature confrontation left V interpreting events as an affair.

runtime.notes: V’s knowledge and Liam’s private plan do not become Lizzy’s knowledge until disclosure. Audio evidence is not proof an engram was actually made.

decisions.description: Liam’s response to a confrontation after evidence.

outcomes.description: V accepted Liam’s payment for discretion.
V explicitly refused the offered payment.

runtime.notes: No inferred refusal from zero payout; require an explicit dialogue result. Taking a bribe and later exposing him are independent choices.

decisions.description: What Lizzy was told about Liam.

outcomes.description: V disclosed the copying proposal.
V told Lizzy the affair version and did not disclose the proposal.

runtime.notes: Store factual disclosure separately from truth known to V. Lizzy may believe the affair report; do not silently upgrade it to the hidden plot.

decisions.description: Whether the second encounter revealed Liam’s death.

outcomes.description: V found Liam dead with Lizzy in the motel.

runtime.notes: Liam’s summoned copy cannot remember events after death. Lizzy knows her own involvement; other characters need a disclosure path.

decisions.description: Whether V helped dispose of Liam’s body.

outcomes.description: V agreed and disposed of the body.
V refused to perform the disposal.

runtime.notes: Agreement alone is not completed disposal. Keep acceptance and completion evidence distinct.

decisions.description: Whether the later braindance is known publicly in this timeline.

outcomes.description: The relevant TV report about Frac-Sure Enough was observed.

runtime.notes: Do not inject the later broadcast before it exists or use its existence to reveal private details to every character automatically.

uncertainties: No source proves a medical diagnosis of cyberpsychosis; avoid presenting speculation as clinical fact.
Early Riot violence can disrupt progression; exact unusual kill branches are not mapped.
